brief: Build a desk command centre that a person sitting in front of it reads at a glance. The viewer is on the side of larger r, so the back of the build is the smallest r. Make two rows. The back row is four full bases, two storeys tall, each with a cover on top, so the tops form a raised deck; stand a 27 inch monitor on that deck, facing the viewer. The front row is four half bases on the ground storey, set in front of the back row, each with a drawer on its cut face so every drawer front faces the viewer, and a half cover on each as a low step. At the left end add two covered bases and put a stack of books on them. At the right end add two bases with divided bins, with pens and markers standing in them, and one covered base carrying a task lamp turned so its head reaches over the bins. On the bench in front of the drawers, far enough out that they can still open, put a keyboard in the middle, a mouse to its right and a phone beyond that, and a mug and a pencil cup to its left. Cap every open face and lock the joints.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
